text: Not many Americans know that their country nearly doubled in size overnight, for less than three cents an acre.
cap: for less than three cents an acre

text: In 1803, Louisiana was not a state. It was a French territory stretching from the Gulf of Mexico to Canada: over two million square kilometres.
cap: stretching from the Gulf of Mexico

text: President Jefferson wanted just one city: New Orleans, the port that controlled the Mississippi River. He was ready to pay up to 10 million dollars for it.
cap: up to 10 million dollars for it

text: But Napoleon had a problem. He was losing Haiti to a slave revolt, and a war with Britain was coming. He needed money, fast.
So he offered the Americans all of it. Every acre of Louisiana, for 15 million dollars.
That is about 380 million dollars today. Roughly 18 dollars per square mile.
The land now covers all or part of 15 states, from Louisiana to Montana.
An acre of Iowa farmland now sells for over 11,000 dollars: about 400,000 times what Jefferson paid.
Still the best real-estate deal in history.
